name: Separation in space
description: Split the conflicting requirements across different places: put the part that needs one property in one location and the part that needs the opposite property in another.
signals: one object must be large and small
one region must be hot and cold
the conflict follows a physical location

name: Separation in time
description: Let the same object satisfy each requirement at a different moment: alternate states, use pauses, or make one property active only during the phase that needs it.
signals: the requirements hold in different process phases
a fast and a slow state are both needed
the conflict appears only during part of the cycle

name: Separation by condition
description: Make the object's behavior depend on a condition: it takes one state under condition A and the opposite state under condition B, without a compromise.
signals: the requirement depends on load, temperature, pressure, or another measurable condition
a single fixed value cannot satisfy both cases

name: Separation in direction
description: Separate the requirements by orientation or direction of action: one direction carries one property, the opposite or transverse direction carries the other.
signals: the conflict depends on which way a force, flow, or signal travels
one axis must be stiff while another must be flexible

name: Separation between system and subsystem
description: Assign opposite requirements to different levels: the system as a whole satisfies one requirement while a subsystem satisfies the other, or the object becomes a nested hierarchy.
signals: the whole and its parts need opposite properties
a monolithic object cannot satisfy both requirements
the conflict disappears once the object is decomposed
